notes.title: Open Beta - New Update: Weather Changes
notes.notes:
[p align="start"]Our latest patch brings weather improvements along with a variety of visual, atmospheric and balance updates.  
[/p][p align="start"][b]Gameplay & Balance[/b][/p][p align="start"]With this patch, we've introduced several gameplay balance adjustments: reducing the build/destruct range to 1.5m (down from 3m), improving door boarding logic, and preventing the diesel-generator gas lid from being stackable under the arm.  [/p][p align="start"][b]Weather[/b][/p][p align="start"]Up until now, the world could shift between six major moods: Wet Haze, Blizzard, Thunderstorm, Hail, Clear Skies and Overcast. We’ve added more subtle weather variations to keep you guessing what might come next.[/p][p align="start"][b]Audio[/b][/p][p]We have also made some tweaks to audio and atmosphere. You can now hear heartbeat signals for dehydration and hunger, tinnitus and gradual world-volume muffling in critical states.[/p][p][b]UI [/b][/p][p]The inventory also got a small update this patch: wet items now show a blue background, so they're easier to spot.[/p][p][/p][p][i]In addition to what’s already mentioned, we’ve made some significant changes to the way we design our camera and lighting, read more in our Dev Blog:[/i][/p][p][url="https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/dev-blog-open-beta-update-002"]https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/dev-blog-open-beta-update-002[/url][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/b44b975d76fcfc5bcd6ec3de0b891682288fed9f.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]Patch Notes: 0.20215 [/p][h3][b]Audio & Atmosphere[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Restored foliage-rustle and rain/hail roof impacts[/p][/*][*][p]Heartbeat now signals dehydration/hunger; intensity scales with risk[/p][/*][*][p]Tinnitus + gradual muffling during critical states
[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Visual & UI[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Wet items show blue background in inventory[/p][/*][*][p]Compass shows on map when in any quick-slot[/p][/*][*][p]Skylight intensity now separates day/night; clearer dusk lighting[/p][/*][*][p]Anti-aliasing toggle added to Settings
[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Gameplay & Balance[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Diesel-generator gas lid no longer stackable under-arm[/p][/*][*][p]Build/destruct range cut to 1.5m (was 3m)[/p][/*][*][p]Door boarding improved: doors are locked when you board a door to a wall with a plank[/p][/*][*][p]Cooking items update calories in real time again[/p][/*][*][p]Medium landing roll slowed 50%; smoother get-up blends[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Items & Inventory[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Bed, oil-lamp, flashlight, walkman, radio collision fixes[/p][/*][*][p]Paper no longer crumples on inspect; lamp glass lights only when on[/p][/*][*][p]Wetness recalculates when moved in hotbar[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Performance & Systems[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Reflections switched to screen-space; minor light tuning[/p][/*][*][p]Fixes for invisible items spawning in shelters[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]World & Environment[/b][/h3][list][*][p]LOD fixes on coat-hanger; outhouse-door collision updated[/p][/*][*][p]Removed floating lamp in cabin; added shelf collisions to jetty & shack[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Open Beta - New Update, New Items
notes.notes: [p]In our latest update we have added three new items alongside various fixes and tweaks.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/270ec2792349d6d77955446ed46e7b1f68cf45dd.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/5c62f9cf0ae7e265501665056fd9d9efd21162cd.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/d838744483e68c7f822710cc416181481c30c9d9.png"][/img][/carousel][p]Find [b]matchbooks[/b] with limited matches to create fire. Matches can fail to light, and you can ruin them by getting them wet. Keep them out of the rain, and don't be surprised if they no longer work after a swim in a river.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Lighters[/b] are a more reliable fire source and a step up from matches, but require fuel. They also double as a weak light source if you dropped or forgot your flashlight. Which you would never do... right?[/p][p]Your trusty [b]Ferro Rod[/b] from previous builds is now a [i]rare item[/i] on every map. [/p][p][/p][p]Also new is the [b]Oil Lamp[/b], which is an alternative to the Flashlight. You can use the Oil Lamp to cast light all around you. Perfect for a cozy camp in the woods, or for building a fire.[/p][p][/p][p]Last but not least, we have made improvements to indications of impending death due to dehydration or malnutrition. You will still die, but less abruptly than before.[/p][p][/p][p]Read more in our Dev Blog: [url="https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/dev-blog-open-beta-update-001"]https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/dev-blog-open-beta-update-001[/url][/p][p][/p][h2]Patch Notes 0.19627[/h2][h3][b]Gameplay & Survival[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Hunger and thirst no longer cause instant death[/p][/*][*][p]Poison now has permanent side effects[/p][/*][*][p]Fire effects on the player have been reduced[/p][/*][*][p]Escape screen has a timer[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Items & Inventory[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added [b]lighter[/b], [b]matchbook[/b], and [b]oil lamps[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Inspecting water containers now shows capacity[/p][/*][*][p]Inventory tooltips are now context-specific (Eat, Drink, Open, etc.)[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]World & Environment[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added audio for rivers[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed rocks so players no longer fall through them[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed hiking stops having higher temperature than the world[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed cabin roofs breaking when first discovered[/p][/*][*][p]More randomness in item spawns, cabin durability, and cabin quality outside exploration zones[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: The Open Beta for Go Wayback! is now available!
notes.notes:
[p]Hi everyone, we’re excited to open up access to the full version of [i]Prologue: Go Wayback![/i] in the form of an [b]Open Beta Playtest[/b] today![/p][p]  [dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/_hU9eG0-Ep8"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]We plan to keep updating the Open Beta with patches and new features over time, until we are ready for an Early Access launch later this year.[/p][p][/p][p]Watch PLAYERUNKNOWN's video message to the community [url="https://youtube.com/shorts/WYULFCO49PQ"]here[/url]![/p][p][/p][p]Add the Open Beta Playtest to your Library via the green Playtest button on the Store page below, and please Wishlist the game if you like the game! It really helps us.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2943740/Prologue_Go_Wayback/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]We are removing the Demo for Go Wayback! for now, as the Open Beta Playtest has no limitation on how many maps you can play and we will be using the Open Beta for public updates going forward.[/p][p][/p][p]We'd love to hear from you what you like and what you'd love to see more of! Leave your comments in the Community Hub ([url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/2943740/discussions/"]here[/url]) or join our Discord ([url="https//community.pp.studio"]here[/url]) to chat with the devs and the community and to stay up to date on the latest news from development.[/p][p][/p][h2]Patch Notes:[/h2][list][*][p][b]Gameplay:[/b] Easier item detection, improved item placement, drink from rivers without entering, new backpack/pot interaction, quickslot map opening, destroyed furniture burns longer.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][b]World:[/b] Storms can break boarded windows, new POIs and cliffs, adjusted indoor temperatures, starter pots now collectible.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Items:[/b] Spoiled/torn gear possible, torn clothing less effective, clothing spawn balance, reduced burnable items, removed prefab fireplaces, various item sound/icon fixes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]UI/Visuals:[/b] New poison icon, blackened fingers in cold, bug fixes for visuals and inspection, corrected labels and player rotation.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Survival:[/b] Added fever mechanic from extreme temperatures.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Misc:[/b] Translation updates and general UI text polish.
[/p][/*][/list][p]\\\\ PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Demo Patch notes: 21/07/2025
notes.notes: [p]We have updated the demo to our latest build. Play across 10 different maps and try to make it to the weather tower![/p][p][/p][h3]FOV Slider[/h3][list][*][p]A Field-of-View slider is now available in settings.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Interactions[/h3][list][*][p]Refilling water containers now uses right-click (RMB) instead of E.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now drink from snowy or, if you're brave, muddy ground.[/p][/*][*][p]New input prompts added. [/p][/*][*][p]You can switch on on-screen prompts for item actions.[/p][/*][*][p]The crosshair now animates when you're unable to carry something underarm.[/p][/*][*][p]A circular progress bar appears when holding to interact. [/p][/*][*][p]Pressing M opens the map if it is in the hotbar.[/p][/*][*][p]Radio and cassette player volume can be changed in game.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Mechanics[/h3][list][*][p]Water containers are refillable from snow, but can also store poisonous water.[/p][/*][*][p]Cooking now reduces food size in your inventory — without lowering calories.[/p][/*][*][p]Wild garlic, wild strawberries, and wild carrots now provide better nutrition. [/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Inventory[/h3][list][*][p]Tin cans are now treated separately by type — they no longer stack into the same hand.[/p][/*][*][p]The flashlight correctly shows whether it's on or off inside shelters.[/p][/*][*][p]Waterproof backpacks now protect stored items from rain and help them dry.[/p][/*][*][p]Backpack sizes are now displayed accurately when inspecting them.[/p][/*][*][p]Clothing insulation has a greater effect on your body temperature.[/p][/*][*][p]More clothes can get damaged. [/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Environment[/h3][list][*][p]Added a miniature landscape diorama inside the Weather Tower showing your journey.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved liquid rendering when holding containers.[/p][/*][*][p]Breakable furniture added — cabin tables and chairs can now be destroyed.[/p][/*][*][p]Map start location and Weather Tower location are now accurately marked.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved rock formations in European Beech areas.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Balancing updates[/h3][list][*][p]Balanced items and consumables available from the starting cabin.[/p][/*][*][p]Balanced wetness from swimming, its more dangerous now.[/p][/*][*][p]Rare waterproof and insulated clothing is even rarer now.[/p][/*][*][p]Balanced getting dry to make it harder. It won't happen until certain conditions are met, e.g. the world temperature is above 2C.[/p][/*][*][p]All shelters now start at the world temperature, its easier to die at the start.[/p][/*][*][p]Fires are harder to maintain in storms, look for rocky outcrops if you are outside. [/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Audio[/h3][list][*][p]New audio mix.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Other Bug Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]Various minor other bug fixes[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Explore 10 New Maps in Updated Demo for Go Wayback!
notes.notes:
[h3]Today we’ve released an [b]update [/b]to our demo for [b]Prologue: Go Wayback! [/b][/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2943740/Prologue_Go_Wayback/
In today’s refresh [b]ten new full maps[/b] take the place of the four map-seeds previously available in the demo. All but one of the new maps are handpicked by our playtest community on Discord, the last one is a favourite from PLAYERUNKNOWN (seed 1,166,976,388). Read on for a sense of what’s waiting beyond the cabin door.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/2913d319aa0eb05610a8561b4b943a7ff594f846.jpg[/img][i]Seed 716741801, photo by 5qu34k.[/i]

This update is part of our ongoing maintenance of the demo, and we’d like to thank everyone who has taken time to send crash reports, bugs and errors, and general impressions. Go Wayback! is both an actively developed game and a technology testbed, your feedback via Steam discussions as well as in our Discord is a huge help in guiding our work.

A common piece of feedback has been that previously Go Wayback! was hard to learn and that the game could do more to help newcomers get situated. While we want the game to be challenging, there is a difference between difficulty and frustration. So, as a quick fix while we explore the issue we’ve added a concise [b]Help screen[/b] that appears on launch—tap [b]H[/b] at any time to bring it back.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/b8ab8fcc95bb5a6f0fe0948f959ecfb7850ff02d.jpg[/img][i]Tap H at any time to see the help screen.[/i]

[url=https://github.com/PLAYERUNKNOWN-Productions/go-wayback-user-support/blob/main/Documents/CHANGELOG.md]Read the full changelog on our User Support Hub[/url]. For those of you looking to learn more about PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions and Go Wayback! we have a [b]community fireside scheduled for July the 16th[/b], come and[url=https://community.pp.studio/] join via our Discord[/url]. We’ve got lots to discuss and its a great opportunity to answer any questions about the future of the game.

To get closer to the development of Go Wayback! ask on Discord about our [b]Outsiders program[/b] where select community members get early access to the full build of Go Wayback! We’ve just started the Outsiders and already its been a great way to get map recommendations for our demos as well as helping find bugs and develop our game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/2d7d0cfc66860119ecf19b816cb3df3e6a507b8d.jpg[/img][i]Seed 776548260, photo by BagelCakes.[/i]

If you haven’t stepped into [b]Prologue: Go Wayback![/b] yet, the demo is free on Steam and Epic Games Store and the door to our [url=https://community.pp.studio/]community Discord[/url] remains open for field notes and future seed ideas. See you out there.

notes.title: Demo for PLAYERUNKNOWN's Prologue: Go Wayback! is out now!
notes.notes:
[p]The demo for [i]Prologue: Go Wayback![/i] is now available. [i]Go Wayback![/i] is a survival roguelike that challenges players to explore and navigate millions of distinct 64km² maps that are different every time you play. [/p][p]This demo lets you play the game, with all of the available survival gameplay systems, across four handpicked maps that cycle with no time limit per round, or number of deaths per session.[/p][p]Explore, experiment, and tell us what works, and what doesn't.

Download the Demo via the green Download Demo button on the Store page:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2943740/Prologue_Go_Wayback/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]In the words of studio founder Brendan “PLAYERUNKNOWN” Greene:[/p][p][i]"Today we are putting a demo of Go Wayback! in players’ hands. Sharing our games during early development is a founding principle of our studio and allows the team to iterate on core systems with player input early. We’re looking forward to your stories, feedback, and bug reports allowing us to shape Go Wayback! together over the coming months before early access launch later this summer."[/i]

Getting early and honest player feedback throughout development is at the core of how we design games at PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions. [/p][p]Our community [url="https://discord.gg/playerunknownproductions"]Discord[/url] offers an open door to our studio and place for our players to see for themselves what we are working on, offer feedback, and have a voice in the future of [i]Go Wayback![/i] [/p][p]As the game is in active development, please head to our [url="https://github.com/PLAYERUNKNOWN-Productions/go-wayback-user-support"]User Support Hub[/url] to troubleshoot bugs and other unexpected problems.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/6bb934f611e0379ef66029519233b138431aac99.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Experience four community-picked maps[/h3][p][i]Go Wayback! [/i]is powered by the studio’s in house [url="https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/guided-generation-in-prologue-ml-generated-landscapes-based-on-game-designer-inpu"]guided generation[/url] terrain system, that leverages machine-learning to generate unpredictable 64km² maps that change every time you play. While the full game features millions of maps, the demo gives access to four community-nominated locations. [/p][p]From foraging-focused forests to near-impossible icy expanses, these picks highlight the scale and diversity of what's possible in [i]Go Wayback![/i][/p][list][*][p]377433344 — suggested by community member lukemars_, who thrives on foraged food.[/p][/*][*][p]1113378335 — nominated by community member GameDevZach: “Really tough.”[/p][/*][*][p]148705728 — shared by community member sleepyente who called it “maybe impossible.” Community member sanyesz proved otherwise, but be ready to run.[/p][/*][*][p]1357488640 — a pick by PLAYERUNKNOWN. Good luck.[/p][/*][/list][p]The game objective is to reach a distant weather tower but, with no time limit, the game encourages free exploration, learning, and experimentation with survival strategies.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/49d588a1fd8897dfbe248708d5d4406a3f93acac.jpg"][/img][/p][p]If you enjoy the demo, please give us a Wishlist and a Follow here on Steam![/p][p]A special thanks to our Discord community who have helped us develop this build over the past months. We would love your feedback so please do [url="https://discord.gg/playerunknownproductions"]join us on Discord to share your thoughts and talk to the devs and the community[/url]. [/p][p]Thanks for being part of the journey.[/p]

notes.title: Join the Go Wayback! Closed Beta (May 7 - May 14)!
notes.notes:
The May Closed Beta begins tomorrow, [b]Wednesday 7th May at 5pm CEST / 8am PT[/b]. [url=discord.gg/playerunknownproductions]Head to our Discord to take part![/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/8fc07ff7adfe19641f8549d9bd3cf4c0bd6f76af.jpg[/img]

Go Wayback! is PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions’ emergent hardcore survival simulation game project. Take on Mother Nature, journey through a procedurally generated wilderness, and find your way to the watchtower to escape. 

Our in-house tech generated a vast number of playable maps and due to the nature of this guided generation there are simply too many scenarios to explore fully on our own. That’s where you come in. We are running regular playtests to gather invaluable feedback to help the development of the game and resolve bugs. [url=https://github.com/PLAYERUNKNOWN-Productions/go-wayback-user-support]Check out our User Support Hub where you can find technical support and track changes.[/url]

[h2]How to get involved in the May Closed Beta[/h2]

[url=discord.gg/playerunknownproductions]Head over to our Discord to sign up and grab your key[/url]. While signups are on a first-come first-served basis, we want to make sure there are enough to go around. If you miss out on this one, you can sign up to get notified of the next one. 

We’re excited to hear your thoughts and insights on Go Wayback!
- The PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions Team

notes.title: Join the April Playtest!
notes.notes:
The April playtest of [b]Prologue: Go Wayback![/b] will run from April 7th through to April 14th. [b][url=https://community.pp.studio/]Head to the official Discord to grab your Steam key and get hands on with the game[/url].[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/d0b1ee717690eb1c485f6d3a2b8446ff30216854.jpg[/img]
[i]Image captured by community member 5qu34k during the March playtest.[/i]

Go Wayback! is a hardcore survival game set in terrain that is produced by our in-house technology. Our tech uses guided generation to produce vast numbers of maps, far too many to completely explore. It is via playtesters that our developers get a deeper sense of these terrains.

We use playtests to find and resolve bugs. So while we do our best to offer a polished experience of the game, there is a non-zero chance that a technical error will pop up during the playtest. In some cases some checks can help out, and to catalogue these fixes we have set up [url=https://go.pp.studio/GoWaybackSupport]our User Support Hub where you can find some technical support for Prologue: Go Wayback![/url]

[h2]How to take part in the March Playtest[/h2]

Our playtest are managed from [url=https://community.pp.studio]our community Discord[/url]. Sign ups will open on Monday April 7th. Once sign ups are open, keys are first come first served. We expect everyone who is able to sign up within the first few hours to be able to grab a key. We want you to try out our game, so we’ll make sure that its not super competitive.

We look really forward to hearing your experiences and insights. We hope to see you on Discord!

—The PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions Team

notes.title: Join our Playtest, Get Hands-on with Prologue: Go Wayback!
notes.notes:
We're excited for the upcoming playtest of our Early Access title, Prologue: Go Wayback! The event starts on the week of March 17th, [url=https://community.pp.studio/][b]head to our Discord to take part[/b][/url].

Our goal with Go Wayback! is to craft a challenging survival experience set within the varied environments produced by our in-house terrain generation technology. Our technology works by producing a vast number of maps, far too many to completely explore. So, it is through the experience of playtesters that our developers get a deeper sense of this world. Sometimes our playtesters discover awesome environments, but they also often find ones that are kind of weird. It’s a fun journey and we’re extremely grateful to all the explorers who help out. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/feb6e4c7e835981642e3c8473f8014e1bd42fcbd.png[/img]
We do our best to offer a smooth experience, but there is a non-zero chance that you will experience a technical error during the playtest. In some cases some checks can help out, and to catalogue these fixes we have set up [url=https://go.pp.studio/GoWaybackSupport]a User Support Hub where you can find some technical support for Prologue: Go Wayback![/url]

During this playtest we’re eager to showcase and validate two main updates:
[list]
[*]We have reworked the forest environment for significantly better performance on a wider variety of systems. As a result we have lowered our playtest min spec and are curious to hear back on how the game is running.
[*]We have introduced a major update to the river generation system—this is just an initial implementation, so there will doubtless be some interesting (read: odd) artefacts, we’re excited to discover those alongside you.[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/322d567e8dd2cdd756fc97214f318c6313827599.png[/img]
On the survival front, we've increased complexity and challenge. Updates to our wetness system mean players will need to work harder to stay dry and warm. Meanwhile we have tweaked weather conditions to pose a greater threat. But we have also added tools and systems to help you navigate these harsher conditions more strategically. Additionally, cabins now function more fully: you'll find useful items, electricity, and a means to dry yourself after exposure to the elements. (Plus, we’ve added a simple end to the game. Good luck getting there though!)

[h2]How to take part in the March Playtest[/h2]

Our playtest are managed from [url=https://community.pp.studio/]our community Discord[/url]. Sign ups will open on March 17th. Once sign ups are open, keys are first come first served. We expect everyone who is able to sign up within the first few hours to be able to grab a key. We want you to try out our game, so we’ll make sure that its not super competitive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/c809711916fa9eb17d4027e4633a3750dd584536.png[/img]
We are hoping to use the data from the March Playtest to make some balance changes to survival difficulty. Advanced the updated river systems based on your feedback. And, confirm improved performance on both minimum and recommended system specifications. We’ll continue adding new features, deepening the survival systems, addressing any bugs discovered in the world, and further enhancing rivers and crossings to enrich exploration.

We look really forward to hearing your experiences and insights. We hope to see you on Discord.

—The PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions Team

notes.title: Dev Blog: How Prologue Unlocks Player-Driven Journeys
notes.notes:
Happy new year to our community!

2025 is a particularly exciting year for our studio, because we are now only a few short months away from the Early Access launch of Prologue: Go Wayback! our upcoming survival game based in an ever-changing machine learning (ML) generated terrain. Which means it is high time we start telling you more about the game. In this series of dev blogs, Scott Davidson, our Creative Director, will give you all the details on how the game is designed, the vision that guides the products we make at PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions, and the practical details of the tech that drives us.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/0af8a25e2297a586cf4461440685d2d059a90ec4.png[/img]
What does it take to build a game where players discover their own journeys? How can gameplay systems create emergent gameplay experiences? At our studio, we are exploring these questions with Prologue. While still in development, Prologue also serves as a test bed for experimental machine learning-driven landscape generation technologies which we feel solve some of the problems of building large worlds but also presents gameplay challenges. During this early phase, our aim is to push the boundaries of emergent design while engaging players with a challenging and immersive experience.

In this blog, we’ll explore the concept of systemic emergent gameplay, highlighting how we are creating a world driven by player choices and offering insights into why we think emergence is cool.

Read more: https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/designing-for-emergence-how-prologue-unlocks-player-driven-journeys/

notes.title: Happy Holidays from PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions
notes.notes:
[b][i]Season's greetings to our community![/i][/b]

As 2024 draws to a close, we want to express our gratitude for our community’s support and engagement. This has been an important time for PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions, marked by [url=https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/preface-undiscovered-world-available-now]the launch of [b]Preface: Undiscovered World[/b][/url] and the [url=https://playerunknownproductions.net/news/wishlist-prologue-go-wayback-on-steam]announcement of [b]Prologue: Go Wayback![/b][/url] Sharing our work with you has been exciting and, honestly, nerve-wracking, but the community’s interest, feedback, and enthusiasm have made it all worthwhile. Thank you!

We’ve prepared a packed blog, reflecting on what we’ve achieved and sharing a glimpse of what’s ahead. [url=https://discord.com/invite/playerunknownproductions]And for those looking to try out [b]Prologue: Go Wayback![/b] we recently announced our second playtest, you can RSVP in our community Discord.[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/2a409c5e77c18ace6f5bd9ee9c6711cb2153ad60.png[/img]

[h1]Prologue Updates[/h1]

[h3]Discord Playtest and Focus Group Feedback[/h3]

We’ve been fascinated by the Prologue playtest and focus group session - ongoing at the time of publishing, but just about to wrap. We can already tell that the written feedback and survey responses offered by players interacting with the early build will shape how we develop the game moving forward. Your honesty and creativity are shaping Prologue in real-time, and we couldn’t be more grateful.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2943740/Prologue_Go_Wayback/ 

We will take a close look at the results of this week’s playtest after the holiday break. And you can expect to hear from us then for a deeper discussion of what we have learned and how we plan to move forward. For now though, we wanted to acknowledge one of the leading positives and one of the leading negatives that we have sensed in chat.
[list]
[*] On the positive side we are over the moon that players have reacted well to the immersion offered by our machine-learning generated terrain and dynamic weather. The love of landscape, and respect for the incredible complexity of the geological and ecological systems that (alongside many others) underwrite it, are at the heart of our studio vision.
[*] Feedback around the interaction points with the game systems has been more middling. And particularly this is linked to the extent to which the game world prompts players and gives them feedback about their actions. The playtest has taught us alot about this, and we’ll have more to say later about how we intend to desiin more intuitive and engaging interactions in the game world.
[/list]These are just preliminary notes and we will return in the new year with a deeper dive into what we learned from this week’s playtest.

[h3]Highlights from User-Generated Content[/h3]
One of our favorite parts of the playtest has been the community’s awesome screenshots. We wanted to take a moment to appreciate a few of the coolest moments from the playtest:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/b21cfd7cb770be6379a528f79937c7f30f99f767.png[/img][i]We loved this image that photographer Mr.Greasy described as “beautiful and brutal” - words that might well make it into our marketing text![/i]

[h2][b][REDACTED][/b][/h2][i]There is a favourite screenshot of ours that we won’t publish! TeZ was our first winner ever, a historic moment! He made it to the end of the game and posted a shot to prove it. But there will be no spoilers here of what that looks like. Alongside all the top 5 finishers, we’re sending TeZ a special limited-run tshirt.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/afc766edab1b1dc4d03622b2fa8a80670201a21f.jpg[/img][i]One of our first playtesters, aeqnx, grabbed this beautiful shot of the woods with the sun peaking through the canopy.[/i]

Thanks again to all our playtesters, the insight you have offered is invaluable in shaping the future of Prologue: Go Wayback!

[h3]Looking Ahead to the New Year[/h3]
[b]Prologue: Go Wayback[/b] has big milestones ahead in 2025. 
[list]
[*] First, we’ll be talking much more about Prologue. Look forward to a series of blogs from our Creative Director Scott Davidson discussing everything from the vision to the nuts and bolts of the game. 
[*] Second, we’re thrilled to announce that the second playtest is scheduled for early next year. The week of Feburary 3rd, to be exact. This will be an opportunity for more of you to get involved, and we can’t wait to hear your thoughts. [url=https://discord.com/invite/playerunknownproductions]You can RSVP for the playtest in our community Discord[/url].
[/list]
[h1]Preface Updates[/h1]

[h3]Reflecting on the Launch[/h3]

It has been just over two weeks since the launch of [b]Preface: Undiscovered World[/b]. Just long enough for us to catch our breath. As many of you know, Preface is a challenging concept—both to build and to understand. Not a game, but a tech demo showing an in-development technology. And the early feedback from the community has been invaluable, even when it was critical.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2820060/Preface_Undiscovered_World/

While the Steam reviews leaned negative overall, this was expected given the tech demo’s early state and the complexity of communicating what the project is, especially to gamers looking for a fun time, or an impressive showcase - neither of which Preface is intended to deliver. However, we don’t want to attribute all challenges to misunderstanding. There’s always room for us to better articulate our vision and make our ideas more accessible and we are still learning more about this.

On a more positive note, the Preface community on Discord has been a source of constant inspiration. The conversations, insights, and camaraderie there have been incredible. Upcoming are some of our highlights from the Discord modding community on Preface.

[h3]Community Highlights and Mods[/h3]
Our community has shown impressive creativity with Preface. Here are some standout contributions:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/ae451623e64bb81b983ba46f6c8836931e9375e5.png[/img][i][b]Planet Radius Mod by Dor:[/b] Dor discovered a way to modify the overall radius of the planet. Interestingly, the radius change operates independently from terrain height or object density, leading to unique effects. For example, making the planet slightly smaller increases the density of objects like trees and rocks, while shrinking it significantly results in dramatic and surreal changes to landscapes and gameplay.[/i]

[previewyoutube=dZnYJ9ruM_I;full][/previewyoutube][i][b]Speed Mod by RoboDanjal:[/b] RoboDanjal increased character movement speed after deducing where user preferences were stored. By examining the reset_preface.bat file, they located the mebla_user_preferences.sqlite database within a Melba folder. Using DB Browser for SQLite, they successfully modified these preferences. 
[list]
[*][url=https://github.com/PLAYERUNKNOWN-Productions/Preface-User-Support/wiki/Controls#extra-controls-and-how-to-enable-them]This mod has been extensively documented by community members in the community wiki.[/url][/list][/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/0af8a25e2297a586cf4461440685d2d059a90ec4.png[/img][i][b]Ray Tracing Activation by YoyoGavri:[/b] By exploring the game files, YoyoGavri managed to activate ray tracing and temporal anti-aliasing on their 10700K/3070 setup, showcasing what’s possible when diving into Preface’s hidden potential.[/i]

We’re continually amazed by what you create, and we’re eager to see more in the future.

[h3]Introducing the GlobeUI Tool[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45333113/7931e69b5832d381b9a2bf933b605901d5cc1cfe.png[/img]
As a modest holiday gift to our Preface community, we’re releasing our own mod! The GlobeUI Tool. This tool allows you to generate waypoint links directly by clicking on the virtual globe, simplifying navigation and interaction. This tool isn’t ours, it’s for the community: We’ve open-sourced the code and released it under an MIT license. You can find the repository here. Feel free to explore, adapt, and build upon it!
[list]
[*][url=https://playerunknown-productions.github.io/preface-globe-navigator/]Here you can find the interface to create deeplink using 3D Planet.[/url]
[*][url=https://github.com/PLAYERUNKNOWN-Productions/preface-globe-navigator]The repo of the above, under MIT license. [/url][/list][h3]A New Open-Source Shader Project[/h3]
In addition to the GlobeUI tool, we’re excited to share an open-source shader project we’ve been working on. This shader is designed to help you achieve dynamic lighting effects, and we’re looking forward to seeing how you integrate it into your own projects. More details will be available soon.
[list]
[*][url=https://github.com/PLAYERUNKNOWN-Productions/preface-shaders]For now you can find the repo of shaders, under Apache 2.0 license here.[/url] [/list]
[h1]Happy Holidays[/h1]
As we wrap up 2024, we’re reminded of how essential your participation is to everything we do. Whether it’s engaging with our releases, contributing feedback, or experimenting with mods, community has been at the heart of our progress. [url=https://discord.com/invite/playerunknownproductions]There’s always a fun conversation ongoing and we’re always open to more feedback, join our Discord to get involved[/url].

From all of us at [b]PLAYERUNKNOWN Productions[/b], happy holidays and best wishes for a wonderful new year. Here’s to more discoveries and innovations in 2025!
